issues.description: validate_conda complects existence, permission, subprocess execution, and identity-matching in one predicate
issues.detail: The function answers four different questions at once: does the path exist, is it executable, does running it succeed, and does its output name a known tool. A caller cannot ask any one of these in isolation, and the empty-string-is-valid shortcut means 'valid' really means 'valid-or-unset'. Decompose into a pure predicate over the stdout string and a small effectful 'probe' that produces the data.

issues.description: custom_conda boolean and conda_path string are two places holding one fact
issues.detail: The configuration models 'which conda to use' as a pair: a flag and a path that is only meaningful when the flag is true. That is place-oriented programming of a single value. One Optional[str] (empty/None means auto-detect, non-empty means use this) is the simple representation; the checkbox is a UI affordance, not a separate fact to persist.

issues.description: Resolution of the conda executable is scattered across find_conda, config lookups, and an inline conditional
issues.detail: argv() now performs a two-step resolution inline: call find_conda, then read two config keys, then decide. The 'what conda should we use' decision is a value worth naming. Pull it into a single resolve_conda_executable() function that returns a path or None and takes the config as data; argv then just consumes the result.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' hardcodes a Windows assumption into a cross-platform setting
issues.detail: On macOS and Linux, conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no .exe extension, so the file picker filter will hide every valid choice. This is incidental complexity leaking from one platform's conventions into the shared config page. Pass platform-appropriate filters as data, or omit the filter entirely.

issues.description: Substring match on --version output will accept any tool whose name contains 'conda' or 'mamba'
issues.detail: Checking `tool in out.decode().lower()` means a binary that prints 'not-conda' or 'mambo-conda-clone v1' passes validation. The fact being asserted is 'this program identified itself as one of {conda, mamba, micromamba}'. Match the leading token of the version string, not a substring anywhere in the output.

issues.description: validate_conda runs an unknown executable with no timeout to decide if a config value is valid
issues.detail: A preferences validator that shells out to an arbitrary user-supplied path on every edit complects UI validation with process execution and trust. At minimum bound it with a timeout; better, separate 'syntactically plausible path' (cheap, pure) from 'actually probes the binary' (explicit, on save), so the preferences page is not silently executing whatever the user typed.

review.summary: The feature is useful and the diff is small, but it ships some classic complecting: a single fact ("which conda to use") is split across a boolean and a string in config, the resolution logic is inlined into argv() instead of being named as its own function, and validate_conda braids four independent checks (existence, executability, subprocess probe, identity match) into one predicate that also treats empty-string as valid. The Windows-only *.exe filter and the loose substring match on --version output are smaller incidental-complexity smells worth fixing. None of this is hard to disentangle — it is easy code that could be made simple.
